items.title: Project finance: phases, sanction and disbursement conditions
items.core_explanation_md:
The **Project Finance chapter** applies from **1 October 2025**, but not to projects whose **financial closure was achieved by that date**.

**Three phases:** **design** (to financial closure) -> **construction** (financial closure to the day before **actual DCCO**, the date of commencement of commercial operations) -> **operational** (from actual DCCO to full repayment).

**Before disbursement**

- **Financial closure** achieved and **original DCCO documented**.
- **Disbursement schedule** tied to **stage of completion** in the loan agreement.
- **Realistic post-DCCO repayment schedule**; tenor including moratorium **not more than 85 per cent of the project's economic life**.
- **One DCCO** across all lenders.
- **All approvals and clearances** (environmental, legal, regulatory) **before financial closure**.
- **Land or right of way:** **50 per cent** for **PPP infrastructure**, **75 per cent** for all other projects; transmission lines as the bank decides.
- **PPP infrastructure:** disbursement only after the **Appointed Date** is declared.
- Disbursal in step with **completion, equity infusion and other sources**; **lender's independent engineer or architect** certifies stages.

**Minimum exposure of an individual bank in under-construction projects**

| Aggregate exposure of all lenders | Individual bank floor |
| --- | --- |
| Up to **Rs 1,500 crore** | **10 per cent** of aggregate |
| Above **Rs 1,500 crore** | **5 per cent or Rs 150 crore, whichever is higher** |

The floors **end after actual DCCO**. A project loan **can turn NPA before DCCO** on the record of recovery. Keep a **project database**, updated within **15 days** of a change.
items.expanded_explanation_md: Resolution of delayed projects (DCCO deferment) is taught with restructuring in a later unit.

self_check.prompt_text: What land or right of way must be available before disbursement for a non-PPP project?
self_check.expected_takeaway: At least 75 per cent.

items.title: Partial credit enhancement (PCE) of bonds
items.core_explanation_md:
A bank may give **PCE** to bonds of **corporates and SPVs** for all types of projects, and to bonds of **non-deposit taking NBFCs with assets of Rs 1,000 crore and above** (including HFCs). The aim is to **lift the bond's rating** so the issuer can borrow on **better terms**.

| Feature | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| **Form** | **Subordinated**, **irrevocable contingent line of credit**, drawn on a **shortfall in cash flows** (may **revolve**); **never a guarantee** |
| **When** | At the **time of the bond issue**; **irrevocable** |
| **Single bank limit** | **50 per cent** of the **bond issue size** |
| **All PCE providers together** | **50 per cent** of the issue size |
| **Rating of the bond** | **Pre-enhanced rating not below BBB minus**, rated by **at least two ECAIs**; reports show **standalone and enhanced** rating |
| **Investing** | The bank **cannot invest** in bonds credit-enhanced by any regulated entity; it may give **other credit** to the issuer |
| **Documents** | A **binding agreement** among **promoter, PCE bank, bondholders (via trustee) and other lenders** |
items.expanded_explanation_md: The courseware's 20 per cent single-bank limit comes from the 2015 and 2016 circulars and is replaced by 50 per cent.

self_check.prompt_text: May PCE be given as a guarantee?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No: it must be an irrevocable contingent line of credit, not a guarantee.

items.title: Take-out financing
items.core_explanation_md:
**Take-out financing** helps a bank that has made a **long-tenor infrastructure loan** avoid an **asset–liability maturity mismatch**: another financial institution agrees to **take over the outstanding loan** on a **pre-determined basis**.

**RBI position:** a loan transfer should move the **economic interest** with **no change to the loan terms**. If terms are **modified** during or after a transfer (for example in take-out financing), the change is **evaluated against restructuring** under the **Resolution of Stressed Assets Directions, 2025**.
items.expanded_explanation_md: The courseware describes IDFC and SBI arrangements; these are not taught.

self_check.prompt_text: What is the main purpose of take-out financing?
self_check.expected_takeaway: To avoid asset-liability mismatch from long-tenor infrastructure loans.

items.title: Documents and the credit officer's checklist
items.core_explanation_md:
Before a bank releases money it must settle: **which documents** to obtain from borrower and guarantors, whether a **charge** is needed on the **primary or collateral security** and **how**, **where it must be registered**, **who holds the security**, **how the loan is disbursed** and **what RBI says**.

**Who signs:** the **borrower** and **guarantors** (so that liability can be proved in court); the borrower also signs the documents creating **charge on the primary security**; an **outside owner of collateral** must **first become a guarantor** and **then** create the charge.

**Checklist for the credit officer**

1. **Properly stamped** (stamp duty differs by **State**).
2. **Date of execution never earlier than the date of stamping**; **date and place** stated.
3. The signers have **authority and capacity** (a partner signs **for the firm**, not personally).
4. The person signs of **free will**.
5. Documents are **filled in before** they are signed.
items.expanded_explanation_md: A blank signed document is a defective document.

self_check.prompt_text: Can a document be executed on a date earlier than the date of stamping?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No: the date of execution should never be earlier than the date of stamping.

items.title: Registration of charges: Registrar of Companies, CERSAI and others
items.core_explanation_md:
**Courseware account (not checked against the Acts):** a company's charge is registered with the **Registrar of Companies within 30 days** of execution; documents needing it go to the **sub-registrar** within the prescribed time; **aircraft** charges also with the **Director General of Civil Aviation**; **ships** with the **Mercantile Marine Department**.

**CERSAI (checked against RBI directions)**

- A **Government company** (section 8, Companies Act 2013) running the **Central Registry** under the **SARFAESI Act 2002**.
- Records are **open to search** by any lender or anyone dealing with the property: it prevents **multiple lending against the same property** and **sale without disclosing the security interest**.
- **Section 23 of SARFAESI:** every security interest transaction is to be **filed**.
- **Gazette notification of 22 January 2016:** file creation, modification or satisfaction of security interest in **(1) immovable property by mortgage other than by deposit of title deeds, (2) hypothecation of plant and machinery, stocks, book debts or receivables (existing or future), (3) intangibles (know-how, patent, copyright, trademark, licence, franchise), (4) under-construction residential or commercial property** (agreement other than mortgage).
- The bank files **current transactions on an ongoing basis**.
items.expanded_explanation_md: The courseware adds that, under the SARFAESI Act, secured creditors enforce securities only if the security interest is filed with CERSAI; the courseware's exception for vehicles on the Vahan site is also its own statement.

self_check.prompt_text: What is the purpose of the CERSAI search facility?
self_check.expected_takeaway: To prevent multiple lending against the same property and sale of a property without disclosure of the security interest.

items.title: Third-party guarantees
items.core_explanation_md:
A bank may ask for **guarantees of third parties** (individuals or other entities) as extra safety.

- **Proprietor or partners:** **no need**: they have **unlimited liability**.
- **Companies and other entities:** owners have **no unlimited liability**, so banks often take **personal guarantees** to make the owners **jointly and severally liable**.

**When a director's personal guarantee helps (courseware)**

| Situation | Why |
| --- | --- |
| **Closely held company** | Binds the **principal members of the group holding shares** (not just managerial directors) |
| **Continuity of management** | A change only with the **lender's knowledge**; **undertaking** that there will be **no change in management without the lender's consent** |
| **Public limited company not rated first class**, advance **unsecured** | Extra comfort |
| **Public limited company** with **weak finances or cash generation** though **secured** | Extra comfort |
| **Delay in creating a charge** | Covers the **interim period** |
| **Subsidiary** with weak finances | **Parent's guarantee** |
| **Interlocking of funds** with group concerns | Group risk |

**No consideration** (commission, brokerage, etc.) is to be paid to guarantors by the borrower, except exceptionally where the **new management's guarantee is essential**.
items.expanded_explanation_md: The courseware ascribes these suggestions to RBI circulars; they are not in the 2025 directions read, so the card is held at needs_review.

self_check.prompt_text: Why is a partner's personal guarantee unnecessary for a partnership loan?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Because partners already have unlimited liability for the firm's debts.

items.title: Types of charge and possession of security
items.core_explanation_md:
**Only the owner of an asset can create a charge on it**; the procedure is the same for **primary** and **collateral** security. The **forms of charge**: **mortgage, hypothecation, pledge, lien, assignment**.

**Possession**

| Method | Who holds the goods |
| --- | --- |
| **Lock and key** (older favoured method) | **Bank** holds the keys of the godown; the borrower pays money into the cash credit account to take delivery |
| **Hypothecation** | The **borrower** keeps possession |
| **Pledge** | Possession **may remain with the borrower** depending on the bank's decision: **constructive possession**, the borrower holds the goods as the **bank's agent** |

What the bank holds affects the **overall risk rating** of the proposal.
items.expanded_explanation_md: Possession matters for inventory because legal enforcement systems are still imperfect.

self_check.prompt_text: Under hypothecation, who retains possession of the goods?
self_check.expected_takeaway: The borrower.

items.title: Disbursal of working capital: cash credit and drawing power
items.core_explanation_md:
In **sole banking** the bank opens a **cash credit account** and **all transactions** are routed through it. Drawings are regulated by **drawing power (DP)** within the sanctioned limit.

**Ideal DP:** current assets minus other current liabilities, from a **full statement**. **Practice:** statements are late, so banks take **monthly statements** of **stocks, book debts and sundry creditors**, apply **margins** (depending on the assessment method) to **stocks and book debts** and **reduce the creditors**.

**DP = stocks (after margin) + book debts (after margin) - sundry creditors**

**Why split into loan and cash credit?** A wholly cash credit limit gives **flexibility** but makes the bank's **fund management hard** (utilisation swings with money market rates) and invites **diversion**. A fixed **loan component** plus a **cash credit** component stabilises use: if the borrower draws little, the **loan account is debited** and the **cash credit shows a credit balance**.
items.expanded_explanation_md: The bank may require the monthly stock and book debt statement before allowing drawings above the last approved DP.

self_check.prompt_text: What is deducted from the margin-adjusted stocks and book debts to find DP?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Sundry creditors (accounts payable).

items.title: Computing drawing power
items.core_explanation_md: A borrower's monthly statement shows stocks of Rs 300 lakh, book debts of Rs 200 lakh and sundry creditors of Rs 80 lakh. The bank stipulates a margin of 25 per cent on stocks and 40 per cent on book debts. The sanctioned cash credit limit is Rs 280 lakh. Find the drawing power and the maximum permitted drawing.

worked_steps.description: Stocks after margin.
Book debts after margin.
DP = stocks + book debts - sundry creditors.
Drawings are limited to the lower of DP and the sanctioned limit.

items.final_answer_with_unit: Drawing power Rs 265 lakh; maximum drawing Rs 265 lakh (below the Rs 280 lakh limit)

self_check.prompt_text: If sundry creditors were Rs 40 lakh, what would the maximum drawing be?
self_check.expected_takeaway: DP would be 225 + 120 - 40 = Rs 305 lakh, above the limit, so Rs 280 lakh.

items.title: The loan system for large working capital borrowers
items.core_explanation_md:
**Who:** borrowers with **aggregate fund based working capital limit of Rs 150 crore and above** from the **banking system** (intra-day facilities excluded).

**Rule:** the **loan component** (working capital loan) must be **at least 60 per cent of the sanctioned fund based limit** (including **ad hoc limits and TODs**). Drawings **up to 60 per cent** come **only from the loan component**; drawings **above it** may be **cash credit or overdraft**.

**How computed:** **exclude** **export credit limits** (pre- and post-shipment) and the **bills limit for inland sales** before bifurcating. **Commercial paper** of the borrower bought by the bank counts in the **loan component** if sanctioned as part of the limit.

**Not applicable to:** **intra-day** credit, **Food Credit Consortium**, **Central Counterparties**, **overseas branches** of the bank.

**In consortium lending** the bifurcation is kept **at individual bank level**.

**The loan itself:** amount and tenor fixed with the borrower; **tenor not less than seven days**; may be split into loans of **different maturities**; repayment in **instalments or bullet**, **rollover** on request, all **subject to the asset classification directions**.
items.expanded_explanation_md: The point is credit discipline: large borrowers pay a fixed loan on a schedule instead of drifting in cash credit.

self_check.prompt_text: What is the minimum share of the fund based working capital limit that must be a loan for a Rs 200 crore borrower?
self_check.expected_takeaway: 60 per cent of the limit (after the exclusions), that is, the loan component.

items.title: Cash credit, current and overdraft accounts: the framework from 1 April 2026
items.core_explanation_md:
| Account or customer | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| **Cash credit (CC)** | A bank may provide it per customer needs, **no restriction** |
| **Current or OD account, banking system exposure under Rs 10 crore** | **No restriction** |
| **Exposure Rs 10 crore or more** | Only a bank with **at least 10 per cent of the banking system's aggregate exposure**, **or of its fund based exposure**, may keep it |
| If **none or only one** bank meets the 10 per cent test | The **two banks with the largest exposure** may keep it |
| If **only one** bank has exposure | **One more bank of the customer's choice**, with the first bank's **NOC** |
| If **no scheduled commercial bank** meets the test | Customer may keep a current account with **one scheduled commercial bank** of choice on **NOCs from all lending banks** |
| Other banks | **Collection accounts only** |

**Collection account:** receipts must be **remitted within two working days** to the **designated** CC, current or OD account (statutory dues and the collecting bank's own dues may be debited first).

**Exempt:** accounts under **FEMA**, accounts required by **statute or a regulator**, and **regulated entities' accounts** for regulated activities.

**Monitoring:** at least **every half-year**. If a bank becomes **ineligible**, it **tells the customer within one month**, and the account is **converted to a collection account or closed within three months**. Accounts are **flagged** in the core banking system and watched **at borrower and account level**.

**No pass-through** use for **third-party** transactions (unless licensed). **Term loans** go **directly to the intended beneficiary** where identifiable rather than through the borrower's account.
items.expanded_explanation_md: This replaces the older courseware idea that a borrower may not open an account elsewhere without the lender's permission.

self_check.prompt_text: A customer's banking system exposure is Rs 8 crore. May any bank keep a current account for them?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Yes: under Rs 10 crore there is no restriction.

items.title: Disbursal of term loans and promoters' equity
items.core_explanation_md:
**Single disbursal** (a machine or ready house): the borrower **deposits the margin**, the loan account is **debited** and the full amount is **remitted to the seller**. If the customer has **already paid the seller**, the bank takes **satisfactory proof** and treats it as part of the **contribution (margin)**. For **personal or consumption loans** the amount may exceptionally be **credited to the customer's account**.

**Project loans:** disbursal follows **progress**: in step with **stages of completion**, **equity infusion** and the other sources agreed at **financial closure**, with the **lender's independent engineer or architect** certifying stages.

**Three ways to bring in promoters' equity (courseware)**

| Method | Equity funding risk |
| --- | --- |
| **Entire contribution upfront** | Lowest |
| **40 to 50 per cent upfront**, balance in stages | Medium |
| **Pro rata** with the bank's disbursements (**ab initio** agreement) | **Greatest** |

Banks should have a **clear policy on the debt equity ratio (DER)**, ensure the **stipulated DER is maintained at all times** and may sequence funding so that **equity funding risk is avoided**.
items.expanded_explanation_md: The risk is that the equity does not arrive after the bank has already lent.

self_check.prompt_text: Which equity method carries the greatest equity funding risk?
self_check.expected_takeaway: The pro rata method, where promoters bring equity as the bank finances the debt.

items.title: Consortium and multiple banking arrangements
items.core_explanation_md:
| | **Sole banking** | **Consortium** | **Multiple banking** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| What | One bank finances | Banks **formally agree** to finance together | Banks lend **separately** with **no formal arrangement** |
| Lead | n/a | A **lead bank** arranges meetings, **assessment, documentation, charge creation, monitoring** | None; banks may share information |

**Information rules (2025 Directions)**

1. **Fresh facilities:** obtain a **declaration** from the borrower about **credit facilities from other lenders**.
2. **Existing borrowers:** seek declarations from those with **sanctioned limits of Rs 5 crore and above**, or where the bank **knows** of other lenders; set up an **information exchange**.
3. **Exchange of conduct information** with other lenders **at least quarterly**.
4. **Regular certification** by a **professional** (preferably **Company Secretary, Cost Accountant or Chartered Accountant**) on **compliance with statutory prescriptions**.
5. Use **credit reports** from **Credit Information Companies**.
6. Put **clauses on exchange of credit information** in loan agreements (confidentiality).

**Unhedged foreign exchange exposure:** the **consortium leader** or the bank with the **largest exposure** has the **lead role** in monitoring it.
items.expanded_explanation_md: These rules were tightened after frauds were linked to poor sharing of information among lenders.

self_check.prompt_text: At what minimum frequency do lenders exchange information on the conduct of a borrower's account?
self_check.expected_takeaway: At least quarterly.

items.title: Syndication of loans
items.core_explanation_md:
**Syndication** shares a **long-term loan** among **two or more banks**: a way of **spreading the risk** of a **large loan**.

1. The borrower gives a **mandate** to one bank, the **lead bank**.
2. The lead bank **approaches other banks** with the details.
3. Each bank **appraises** the proposal under **its own policy and risk appetite** and **decides**.
4. **Common terms** are agreed in a **meeting of participating banks** arranged by the lead bank.
5. The lead bank normally charges the borrower a **syndication fee**.

**Contrast with consortium:** a consortium usually shares **working capital** finance with a **formal arrangement** and a lead bank that monitors; syndication is mostly for **term loans**, arranged **loan by loan**.
items.expanded_explanation_md: In both, the lead bank acts as the liaison.

self_check.prompt_text: What does the lead bank in a syndication usually earn from the borrower?
self_check.expected_takeaway: A syndication fee.

items.title: Straight through processing and credit underwriting engines
items.core_explanation_md:
**STP (credit underwriting engine):** **full automation** of the loan sanction cycle, **application to disbursement**, with **little or no manual interference**.

**Why banks use it:** **uniform** approach, sanction and documentation; **speed** with **less overhead**; **location is irrelevant**; staff freed for **complex** cases. It began with **personal segment loans** (home, car, personal) and now serves **MSME and other commercial lending**.

**How it works:** the lender's **loan policy** is coded as **rules and parameters** (ratios, scores, LTV, EMI/NMI); **data feeds** come from **KYC**, **ownership documents**, **charge history**, **credit information companies** and **Aadhaar**-linked verification.

**Risk mitigation:** a sanction is made only when **industry, business, financial, management, default, country and exchange risks** are all identified; STP integrates **third-party data**.

**Machine lending:** decisions rest on **algorithms**; parameters must stay **flexible** as conditions change.

**Omissions and commissions:** rule-based processing nearly **removes omissions** and gives **fewer chances for commissions** (biased or fraudulent judgement).

**Limits:** a **wrong data feed** produces a **chain of bad outputs**; STP must be **synchronised with the core banking solution**; it is **not a panacea**.
items.expanded_explanation_md: Garbage in, garbage out: the quality of the initial data decides the quality of the decision.

self_check.prompt_text: What is the main weakness of an STP system the courseware warns about?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Error in the data fed: every later step builds on it and produces a chain of bad outputs.

items.title: Why credit is monitored: the loan review mechanism
items.core_explanation_md:
Even with good appraisal, documents and security, **default risk remains** because the **assumptions of appraisal go stale**. **Credit control and monitoring**, often called the **Loan Review Mechanism (LRM)**, has three aims:

1. **Right use of funds:** detect and stop **diversion** out of the business or **unauthorised use** within it.
2. **Business on projected lines:** notice **deterioration** from the appraisal projections and act, **in consultation with the borrower**, so the business **stays viable**.
3. **Hard action if needed:** if deterioration continues, decide whether to **recall the advance** or **seize the security**. **Delay** lowers the **chance and amount of recovery**.
items.expanded_explanation_md: Monitoring protects both the borrower's viability and the bank's security.

self_check.prompt_text: What is the LRM also called?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Credit control and monitoring (the Loan Review Mechanism).

items.title: Monitoring tools, part 1: accounts, statements and audits
items.core_explanation_md:
RBI advises banks **not to rely only on CA certificates or borrower certificates** about end use. If a certificate is **wrong**, the bank may **withdraw the facilities** and take **legal action**.

| Tool | What it tells you |
| --- | --- |
| **(a) Conduct of the account** | **Danger signs:** **frequent overdrafts**, **returned cheques or bills**, **late stock or receivables statements**, **low turnover**, **transactions routed through another bank**, **late interest or instalments**, **devolved LCs**, **invoked guarantees**. **Response:** more **godown inspections**, **sale proceeds routed through the bank**, **pledge in place of hypothecation** |
| **(b) Periodic statements** | **Monthly stock and receivables statements** feed **drawing power**; scrutinise **non-moving stocks** and **old receivables** (normally **over six months** are moved to **non-current assets** and **excluded** from DP); **cross-check** at inspections |
| **(c) Stock or receivables audit** | For **medium and large accounts** where normal inspection cannot verify, or stocks sit at **several locations**; checks **reliability of statements** |
| **(d) Financial statements and auditors' report** | Usually **annual**; show **use or diversion of funds**, **financial health**, **debt realisation**, **profitability**; used at **renewal** |
items.expanded_explanation_md: The courseware treats six months as the usual age at which receivables are excluded from drawing power.

self_check.prompt_text: Which sign is an unsatisfactory feature of the conduct of an account: routing of transactions through another bank or high turnover?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Routing transactions through another bank (high turnover is a favourable sign).

items.title: Monitoring tools, part 2: visits, interaction, reports and board nominee

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| **(e) Periodic visits and inspections** | Impression of **activity level**; verify **stocks and other assets charged to the bank**; confirm the bank's **charge is prominently displayed** |
| **(f) Interaction with select creditors and debtors** | Cross-check **business reality** |
| **(g) Scrutiny of books and of accounts with other banks** | Detect **diversion** and **window dressing** |

items.title: Credit audit
items.core_explanation_md:
**Credit audit** is an **internal staff review** of the bank's **credit functions**, checking **compliance with sanction and post-sanction processes**, important for **large value accounts** (courseware, from RBI's 2002 Guidance Note; held at needs_review).

**Objectives:** better **portfolio quality**; review **sanction process and compliance** of **large loans**; **feedback on regulatory compliance**; **independent review of credit risk assessment**; spot **early warning signals** and suggest **remedies**; recommend action to improve **credit quality, administration and staff skills**.

**Scope**

- **Portfolio review:** quality of **credit and investment portfolio**; reduce **concentrations**.
- **Loan review:** **all fresh proposals and renewals** (within **3 to 6 months** of sanction); **accounts at or above a cut-off**; a **random 5 to 10 per cent** of the rest; **sister, group and associate concerns** even below the cut-off.

**Frequency:** **high risk 3 months**, **average risk 6 months**, **low risk 1 year**.

**Procedure:** done **at the branch that appraised the advance** where the main limits are available; **no visit to the factory or office** needed; reports on conduct of **allocated limits** are called from the other branches.
items.expanded_explanation_md: The department may be a separate credit audit unit or sit in the Inspection and Audit Department.

self_check.prompt_text: Must credit auditors visit the borrower's factory?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No: credit audit is done on site at the appraising branch without visiting the factory or office.

items.title: Credit risk evaluation: the 2025 Directions
items.core_explanation_md:
| Rule | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| **Independent appraisal** | The bank appraises **independently and objectively**; it does **not rely on reports from outside consultants**, especially the **borrower's in-house consultants** |
| **Sensitivity tests** | **Scenario analysis**, especially for **infrastructure**: **delays and cost overruns**, to judge viability when deciding on **DCCO deferment or restructuring** |
| **Promoters' equity** | Check **source and quality** of equity; **parent debt must not be infused as equity** of a subsidiary or SPV (**multiple leveraging** hides the debt equity ratio) |
| **Credit Information Reports** | Loan policy must provide for **CIRs from one or more Credit Information Companies** |
| **Consumer credit** | **Board approved limits** by sub-segment; **limits for all unsecured consumer credit**, watched by the **Risk Management Committee** |
| **Review and end use** | Follow the specified circulars on **ad hoc, short review and renewal** and **end use monitoring** |

items.title: Drawing power statements and review of limits
items.core_explanation_md:
**Working capital accounts**

1. Drawings must be **covered by adequate current assets**.
2. **Drawing power** comes from a **current stock statement**.
3. For **large borrowers**, the stock statement used **must not be older than three months**.
4. Outstanding based on a **stock statement older than three months** is **deemed irregular**.

**Review of limits**

- **Regular and ad hoc limits** are **reviewed or regularised not later than three months** from the **due date** or the **date of ad hoc sanction**.
- If **financial statements are missing**, show **evidence** that **renewal is under way**; a **delay beyond six months is not desirable** as a general discipline.
- **Avoid frequent, repeated ad hoc or short reviews** without good reason.
- **Capture review data** in core banking or MIS and bring the process under **concurrent or internal audit**.
- The **Board policy** covers **appointment of external agencies for stock audit and valuation of collateral** and the **methodology and periodicity** of review.
items.expanded_explanation_md: Older stock statements make drawing power unreliable, which is why the account becomes irregular.

self_check.prompt_text: How old may a stock statement be for DP of a large borrower?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Not older than three months.

items.title: Large NPAs: stock audit, valuation of collateral and advocates' certificates
items.core_explanation_md:
For **NPAs with a balance of Rs 5 crore and above**:

- **Stock audit every year** by **external agencies** appointed under **Board approved guidelines** (to make **stock valuation reliable**).
- **Immovable property collateral** **valued once in three years** by **valuers** appointed under Board approved guidelines.

**Advocates and valuers:** the bank **seeks an explanation** from advocates who **wrongly certify clear legal title** and from valuers who **overstate** security value (negligence or connivance). If there is **no satisfactory reply within one month**, it may **report their names to the Indian Banks' Association**.

**Board duty:** arrest **deteriorating asset quality**; recognise problems early, using **CRILC** (the Central Repository of Information on Large Credits).
items.expanded_explanation_md: The Rs 5 crore threshold applies to the NPA balance, not the original limit.

self_check.prompt_text: How often must collateral of a large NPA be revalued?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Once in three years.

items.title: The three risks of banking and what credit risk is
items.core_explanation_md:
| Risk | What it is | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Operational** | Losses from **failure of people or process or both** | **Fraud**, disruption by **floods** |
| **Market** | Losses from **adverse market movements** | **Interest rate**, **exchange rate** changes |
| **Credit** | **Non-payment** by the borrower | See below |

**Credit risk**

- **Fund based:** the borrower does **not pay principal and interest** as agreed.
- **Non-fund based:** the customer does **not reimburse the bank** (fully or partly) when a **guarantee is invoked** or an **LC devolves**.
- It comes from the borrower's **unwillingness or inability** to meet financial commitments.
items.expanded_explanation_md: Loss from fraud is classed by the courseware as an operational risk, not a credit risk.

self_check.prompt_text: Is loss to the bank from fraud a credit risk?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No: it is an operational risk.

items.title: Factors that affect credit risk
items.core_explanation_md:
| | **External factors** | **Internal factors** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Origin** | **Environment** that hits the customer's business | The **bank's own** policies and practices |
| **Examples** | **Exchange rate and interest rate swings**, **Government policies**, **protectionist policies of other countries**, **political risk** | **Concentration** in a segment or region, **excessive lending to cyclical industries**, **ignoring the purpose of the loan**, **faulty loan and repayment structuring**, **weak loan policy**, **poor appraisal and monitoring**, **no efficient recovery machinery** |
| **Effect** | **Indirect:** they impair the **customer's** business | Direct result of **weaknesses at the bank** |

**Another view**

- **Portfolio risk** (external environment): **concentration risk**, **industry risk**.
- **Transaction risk** (internal environment): **default risk**, **spread risk**, **downgrade risk**, **recovery risk**.
items.expanded_explanation_md: External factors look like market risks but affect the bank through its customers.

self_check.prompt_text: Is excessive lending to cyclical industries an internal or external factor?
self_check.expected_takeaway: An internal factor.

items.title: Mitigating credit risk: macro and micro steps
items.core_explanation_md:
The aim is to keep credit risk **within acceptable levels** and **maximise the risk-adjusted return**.

| Level | Steps |
| --- | --- |
| **Macro** (whole portfolio) | **Frequent review of norms**; **internal limits** on aggregate commitments to **sectors or industries** so exposure is **spread evenly**; periodic review of **exposure norms for single and group borrowers** and of **discretionary powers**; policies on **stress resolution** (**rectification, restructuring, compromise, recovery, write off**) and **stress tests** |
| **Micro** (each proposal) | **Appraisal standards**; **sanction and delivery process**; **monitoring and review** of individual proposals; **collateral security**; **personal guarantees**; **escrow mechanism**; **corporate guarantee of holding company**; **credit rating and scoring** |
| **Dispersion for large accounts** | **Consortium or multiple banking**; **derivatives** such as **credit default swaps** |
items.expanded_explanation_md: Macro steps shape the book; micro steps protect each loan.

self_check.prompt_text: Is an escrow mechanism a macro or micro level step?
self_check.expected_takeaway: A micro level step.

items.title: Why a credit rating is made
items.core_explanation_md:
The **risk** in a proposal depends on its **own features**: two similar projects with **different promoters**, or two different projects with the **same promoters**, can carry **different risks**. The risk is **measured and often quantified as a rating**.

**Objectives of rating**

1. **Decide:** **accept, reject, or accept with modifications or special covenants**.
2. **Price:** fix the **rate of interest**.
3. **Macro view:** classify the **whole portfolio** by ratings of individual accounts, to **assess provisioning**, support **management decisions** and **review the loan policy**.
items.expanded_explanation_md: A rating therefore links risk to price and to portfolio management.

self_check.prompt_text: Name the three objectives of a credit rating.
self_check.expected_takeaway: To decide on acceptance, to determine pricing, and to support macro evaluation of the portfolio.

items.title: Internal and external ratings, and the rating agencies
items.core_explanation_md:
**Internal rating** is built by the bank on **its own data and risk perceptions** (**rating the risk for internal use**). **External rating** is given by an **accredited credit rating agency**; where a facility has an **eligible agency's rating**, its **risk weight** (for capital adequacy) is based on that rating.

**Domestic agencies whose ratings banks may use (RBI)**

1. **Acuite Ratings and Research**
2. **Brickwork Ratings India**
3. **CARE Ratings**
4. **CRISIL Ratings**
5. **ICRA**
6. **India Ratings and Research**
7. **INFOMERICS Valuation and Rating**

**International (where specified):** **Fitch, Moody's, Standard and Poor's**.

**Consistency rule:** use the **chosen agency consistently** for each type of claim, for **risk weighting and risk management**; **no cherry picking** of ratings from different agencies and **no arbitrary change** of agency.
items.expanded_explanation_md: The courseware lists SMERA, which is now Acuite.

self_check.prompt_text: May a bank pick the best rating from several agencies for the same claim?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No: cherry picking is not allowed.

items.title: The methodology of a credit scoring model
items.core_explanation_md:
Each bank has its **own rating model**, but all share a **common feature**: **scores** are given for **different perceived risks**, each with its own **weightage**, and the **sum of the scores** decides the **risk rating** of the proposal.

**Broad risk areas scored**

1. **Promoters and management**, and the **securities available**;
2. **Financial aspects** (analysis of **financial statements**);
3. **Business, industry or project** risks.

| Rating | Basis for |
| --- | --- |
| **Borrower Rating (BR)** | **Probability of Default (PD)** |
| **Facility Rating (FR)** | **Loss Given Default (LGD)** |

Ratings (**external credit rating, borrower rating, facility rating**) are **reviewed periodically** and **upgraded, downgraded or kept** as the **facts and environment** justify.
items.expanded_explanation_md: Expected loss follows from PD, LGD and the exposure at default.

self_check.prompt_text: Which rating is the basis for assigning the Loss Given Default?
self_check.expected_takeaway: The Facility Rating.

items.title: Scoring a proposal and estimating expected loss

Maximum score.

items.title: Credit derivatives: credit default swaps and credit linked notes
items.core_explanation_md:
**Credit derivatives** hedge the **risk in a credit asset** **without transferring the asset**. Like **insurance**, the hedge **costs** something: if the feared event does not happen, the return is **lower than without the hedge**. Older techniques: **financial guarantees, collateral security, credit insurance**.

| | **Credit default swap (CDS)** | **Credit linked note (CLN)** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Who pays whom | The **lending bank (protection buyer)** pays a **premium** to the **protection seller** | The **bank (risk seller)** pays a **regular premium** to the **risk buyer**, usually an **SPV** |
| Reference | The **issuer on whom protection is given** is the **reference entity** | Notes are **linked to the underlying credit** |
| Funding | None up front | **Investors buy the notes**; the SPV buys **high quality securities** with the money |
| On default | Bank **hands over the debt instrument** and gets paid | **Securities are used to pay the bank**; investors lose |
| Documents | Usually the **ISDA** standard; **ISDA defines credit events** (bankruptcy, failure to pay, restructuring, obligation acceleration) | Fixed or floating return to investors during the life of the note |
items.expanded_explanation_md: The courseware's remarks on RBI's restrictions on credit derivatives were not checked and are not taught.

self_check.prompt_text: In a CDS, who is the protection buyer?
self_check.expected_takeaway: The lending bank holding the credit exposure.

items.title: RBI guidelines on credit risk management
items.core_explanation_md:
From the **Credit Risk Management Directions, 2025** and the **IRACP Directions, 2025**:

1. **Follow the Guidance Note on Credit Risk Management** and do **independent and objective credit appraisal** in all cases: **do not depend on reports from outside consultants**, especially the **borrower's in-house consultants**.
2. Run **sensitivity tests and scenario analysis**, especially for **infrastructure**: **delays and cost overruns**.
3. Ascertain the **source and quality of promoters' equity**; make sure **parent debt is not infused as equity** of a subsidiary or SPV (**multiple leveraging** camouflages the **debt equity ratio**).
4. **Board oversight:** **arrest deteriorating asset quality**; improve **credit risk management**; **recognise problems early** using **CRILC**.
items.expanded_explanation_md: Items on wilful defaulters and Director Identification Numbers in the courseware list are not taught here.

self_check.prompt_text: Which repository should banks use for early recognition of problems in large accounts?
self_check.expected_takeaway: CRILC, the Central Repository of Information on Large Credits.

items.title: The credit information system: CICs and CRILC
items.core_explanation_md:
**Why:** to **alert lenders** to borrowers who have **defaulted elsewhere** and to **stop fresh NPAs** building up, through an **efficient system of credit information on borrowers**.

| | **Credit Information Companies (CICs)** | **CRILC** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What | Companies that **collect, process and share** credit information on borrowers of credit institutions | A **repository set up by the RBI** to **collect, store and disseminate** credit information on **large credits** |
| Who reports | **Credit institutions**, which are **members** of CICs | **Banks**, for borrowers above an **aggregate exposure threshold** (fund based and non-fund based) |
| Content | Credit history, **existing and past exposures** | Includes **classification of an account as SMA** |
| Basis | **Credit Information Companies (Regulation) Act, 2005** (courseware) | RBI instructions |

Banks should **make greater use of CIC reports**, and the **loan policy must provide for obtaining Credit Information Reports** from one or more CICs.
items.expanded_explanation_md: The courseware gives thresholds and fee limits from 2014 and 2015 circulars; they are not taught.

self_check.prompt_text: Who set up CRILC?
self_check.expected_takeaway: The Reserve Bank of India.

items.title: Credit default, stressed assets and the provision coverage ratio
items.core_explanation_md:
**Credit default** is the **inability or unwillingness** of a customer or counterparty to meet a commitment.

| Business | What a default looks like |
| --- | --- |
| **Direct lending** | **Principal or interest** not paid as per terms |
| **Guarantees and LCs** | Constituent does **not provide funds** when the liability **crystallises** |
| **Treasury** | Contract payments **not forthcoming** or **cease** |
| **Securities trading** | **Funds or securities settlement** not effected |
| **Cross-border exposure** | The **sovereign stops** availability or free transfer of **foreign currency** |

**Stressed assets:** default has **already happened** or faces a **reasonably certain prospect** of default. Example: a **term loan for an industrial project whose implementation was abandoned** is stressed **even though no instalment is due yet**.

**Provision Coverage Ratio (PCR) = provisioning / gross NPAs**: how much the bank has set aside against loan losses.
items.expanded_explanation_md: Stress is recognised before NPA status: the SMA categories in the framework card capture early stages.

self_check.prompt_text: What is PCR?
self_check.expected_takeaway: The ratio of provisioning to gross non-performing assets.

items.title: How a wilful defaulter is identified
items.core_explanation_md:
**Principles:** look at the **track record**, not isolated transactions; the default must be **intentional, deliberate and calculated**.

| Step | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | **Identification Committee** examines the evidence |
| 2 | **Show-cause notice** with all material; submissions within **21 days** |
| 3 | Proposal to the **Review Committee** with **written reasons** |
| 4 | Person has **15 days** to give a **written representation** |
| 5 | **Personal hearing** by the Review Committee |
| 6 | **Reasoned order** communicated. No right to a **lawyer** (in-house process) |

**Committees:** **Identification:** a **whole-time director (not the MD and CEO)** plus **two senior officials**. **Review:** the **MD and CEO** plus **two independent or non-executive directors**; **different people** from the Identification Committee.

**Non-executive, independent or nominee directors** are **not** wilful defaulters unless it is **conclusively shown** that the default had their **consent or connivance**, or they **knew from board minutes** and **did not record objection**.

**When:** examine wilful default in all **NPAs of Rs 25 lakh and above**; complete classification **within six months** of NPA classification.
items.expanded_explanation_md: The 2025 text fixes the six-month limit from the NPA date.

self_check.prompt_text: Within how many days of the show-cause notice must the person respond?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Within 21 days.

items.title: Penal measures and reporting on wilful defaulters
items.core_explanation_md:
**Penal measures**

- **No additional credit** to the wilful defaulter or **associated entities**; the bar **lasts one year after removal** from the list.
- **No credit for new ventures for five years after removal**.
- **Restructuring** only as the Resolution of Stressed Assets Directions allow.
- **Covenant:** the borrower will **not induct a person from the list** on its board or management; **no renewal, enhancement, fresh credit or restructuring** while such a person remains.
- **Associated entities:** a **subsidiary, joint venture or associate**; for a **natural person**, entities where he is **promoter, director or in charge of management**.
- **Guarantors** who refuse to pay on demand may be classified too; **group companies** whose guarantees are not honoured are considered.

**Reporting (to all Credit Information Companies, monthly)**

- **Large defaulters** (Rs 1 crore and above; suit-filed, or doubtful or loss).
- **Wilful defaulters** (suit-filed and non-suit-filed).
- **Removal** within **30 days** after the outstanding falls below **Rs 25 lakh**, **except** in a **compromise**: the name stays until the **compromise amount is fully paid**.
- Include the **Director Identification Number (DIN)** so similar names are not wrongly denied credit; at appraisal check directors, guarantors and persons in charge in the lists by **DIN or PAN**, confirming identity from **independent sources**.

**After a resolution that changes management and control** (IBC or the resolution framework): the borrower and its promoters and directors are **removed from the list** and penal measures on the **new entity** cease; the **one- and five-year bars continue for erstwhile promoters**.
items.expanded_explanation_md: Before a bank transfers a defaulted loan of Rs 25 lakh and above, it must test for wilful default first.

self_check.prompt_text: For how long after removal from the list is a new venture barred from bank credit?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Five years.

items.title: Restructuring: what it is and when it is allowed
items.core_explanation_md:
If the default is **not wilful**, the unit is **viable** and the promoter is **keen to continue**, banks **restructure** on revised cash flow estimates.

**Restructuring:** the bank, **for economic or legal reasons relating to the borrower's financial difficulty**, grants **concessions it would not otherwise consider**: change in **payment period, amount or instalment, rate of interest**; **roll over**; **additional credit** for an account in default to cure it; **enhanced limits**; **compromise** where payment takes **more than three months**.

**Concessions the courseware lists:** **elongation**, **fresh moratorium**, **balloon repayment**, **cut in pricing and margin**, **fresh facilities**, **capitalisation** of unpaid interest and instalments, **conversion of working capital outstanding into term loans**, and **devolved LCs and invoked guarantees converted to medium or long term loans**.

**Conditions:** **no restructuring unless financial viability is established** and repayment is **reasonably certain**. Restructuring **without checking cash flows** is **evergreening** and invites supervisory action.

**Supervisory action:** any step meant to **conceal the true status** of accounts or **evergreen** stressed accounts brings **higher provisioning** and **monetary penalties**.
items.expanded_explanation_md: Restructuring normally needs the borrower's consent and a changed loan agreement.

self_check.prompt_text: Is a compromise paid over six months a restructuring?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Yes: a compromise where the time for payment exceeds three months is treated as restructuring.

items.title: Rectification, restructuring and recovery
items.core_explanation_md:
| Route | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Rectification** | **Regularisation** (persuade the borrower to pay the overdue and stay prompt) and **exit** |
| **Restructuring** | **Rephasing or realignment**, **concessions and relaxations**, **additional finance** |
| **Recovery** | **Legal action**, **compromise**, **write off** |

**Exit:** the bank's **first effort**, but possible only if stress is **detected very early**, so the borrower can **move to a bank with a different risk appetite**. In **consortium or multiple banking**, others may take the exiting bank's share; in **sole banking** it is **hard**.

**Tactics for exit:** **withdraw concessions and priorities**, **enforce covenants in letter and spirit**, **ignore pleas for excess drawing**, **reduce limits**, **decline excess drawings**.

The **timing and choice** of strategy are decisive for recovery.
items.expanded_explanation_md: Early detection keeps all three routes open.

self_check.prompt_text: Which route is the bank's first effort in a stressed account?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Rectification: regularisation or exit.

items.title: Recovery forums
items.core_explanation_md:
| Forum | Courseware account | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Civil Court** | Recoverable amount **below Rs 20 lakh**; plaint signed by the authorised official; preliminary decree, payment within **six months**, execution within **12 years** | statutory limits as the courseware states (needs_review) |
| **Debt Recovery Tribunal (DRT)** | **Rs 20 lakh and above**; NBFCs with assets above **Rs 100 crore** can file; **summary** procedure | statutory (needs_review) |
| **Lok Adalat** | Settlement forum under the **Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987** | RBI limits below |
| **SARFAESI Act, 2002** | Enforce **security interest without courts or tribunals**: **demand notice of 60 days**, **possession and sale**; **CERSAI** records; registered secured creditors have **priority** | statutory (needs_review) |
| **IBC, 2016** | **Single law** on insolvency and bankruptcy; an effective tool for banks | taught in the next unit |

**RBI limits for Lok Adalats**

- Civil Court Lok Adalats: cases up to **Rs 20 lakh**.
- **DRT or DRAT Lok Adalats:** a bank may take part for cases of **Rs 10 lakh and above**.
- Banks are **encouraged** to use Lok Adalats for **personal loans, credit card loans and housing loans of less than Rs 10 lakh**.
items.expanded_explanation_md: The courseware says banks may refer DRT Lok Adalat cases irrespective of amount; the 2025 Directions say Rs 10 lakh and above.

self_check.prompt_text: Up to what amount may a bank refer cases to a Lok Adalat organised by a civil court?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Rs 20 lakh.

items.title: Compromise settlements
items.core_explanation_md:
**Objective:** **maximise recovery at minimum expense**, in the bank's best interest. **Not a right**: a **discretion** exercised on **commercial judgement**.

**Courseware principle:** the **present value of the compromise offer** must be **higher than** the **present value of the realisable value of the security**.

**Treated as restructuring:**

- payment of the settlement amount takes **more than three months**;
- a **part settlement**;
- an arrangement where the bank puts **claims on contingent future recoveries** on its balance sheet.

**Governance**

- Board policy: **process** (minimum ageing, fall in collateral value), **staff accountability**, **permissible sacrifice**, **valuation** of security.
- **Approval** one **level above** the sanctioning authority; **anyone who sanctioned the loan** takes **no part** in approving the compromise.
- **Fraud or wilful default** borrowers: **Management Committee of the Board** (or the Board where the Management Committee made the original approval).
- **Pending suit:** a **consent decree** is needed.
- **Cooling period** before fresh exposure: floor of **12 months** (other than farm credit).
- **Reporting** at least **quarterly** to the next higher authority; to the **Board** for approvals by the **MD and CEO** or a Board committee.

A compromise with a fraud or wilful default borrower is allowed **without prejudice to criminal proceedings and penal measures**.
items.expanded_explanation_md: A compromise ends the bank's relationship with the borrower; a restructuring continues it.

self_check.prompt_text: What is the floor for the cooling period before fresh exposure to a borrower after a compromise (other than farm credit)?
self_check.expected_takeaway: 12 months.

items.title: Technical write-off and write off
items.core_explanation_md:
**Technical write-off:** NPAs stay **outstanding in the borrower's account** but are **written off for accounting only**, **fully or partly**, with **no waiver of claims** and no harm to **recovery**.

- It **cleanses the balance sheet** of debts that are **unrecoverable** or whose recovery would **cost too much**.
- The **borrower's legal obligation** and the **costs of default** to the borrower are **unchanged**.
- **Partial technical write-off:** prudential rules (**provisioning, asset classification**) apply with reference to the **original exposure**; the **provision plus the amount written off** must meet the **requirement on the gross value**.
- **Cooling period** after a technical write-off: as per **Board policy**.

**Write off (courseware):** when **recovery efforts are exhausted**, the outstanding is written off **against the provision**, with any **excess charged to profit and loss**. It **does not end the borrower's liability**; the bank may **appropriate any later recovery**. It is **not the first choice** but saves **time and time-value** when done at the right time.
items.expanded_explanation_md: Technical write-offs are reported quarterly to a higher authority along with compromise settlements.

self_check.prompt_text: Does a technical write-off waive the borrower's liability?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No: claims against the borrower continue and recovery is not prejudiced.

items.title: Early recognition of stress: SMA categories and CRILC
items.core_explanation_md:
A bank recognises **incipient stress immediately on default** by classifying accounts as **special mention accounts (SMA)**.

| | **Loans other than revolving** (overdue principal, interest or other amount) | **Cash credit and overdraft** (continuous excess over limit or drawing power, whichever is lower) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **SMA-0** | **Up to 30 days** | **None** |
| **SMA-1** | **More than 30 and up to 60 days** | **More than 30 and up to 60 days** |
| **SMA-2** | **More than 60 and up to 90 days** | **More than 60 and up to 90 days** |

**Scope:** all loans **including retail**, except **agricultural advances** on **crop season** norms; **any size of exposure**.

**CRILC reporting:** SMA status and other credit information for all borrowers with **aggregate exposure of Rs 5 crore and above**, **monthly**; plus a **weekly report** of defaults by borrowers with Rs 5 crore and above **every Friday**.

**Signs of financial difficulty** (in the Board policy): a **default** (whatever the reason), a **probable default**, **delisting** threats, **insufficient cash flow**, **NPA or near-NPA** status, internal **rating** deterioration. **Financial difficulty may exist even without arrears.**
items.expanded_explanation_md: Beyond 90 days the account is an NPA; the SMA bands are the last warning stages.

self_check.prompt_text: How many days of continuous excess over the lower of limit or drawing power puts a cash credit account in SMA-2?
self_check.expected_takeaway: More than 60 and up to 90 days.

items.title: Review period and inter-creditor agreement
items.core_explanation_md:
**Review Period:** **30 days** from the **date of default** or credit event. In it the **specified lenders jointly** review the account and decide the **resolution strategy**. A bank may also start **insolvency or recovery** proceedings. Banks should even start before default: default is a **lagging indicator**.

**Specified lenders:** **commercial banks** (including small finance banks, excluding payments banks, local area banks and RRBs); **all India financial institutions**; **deposit-taking NBFCs** (not HFCs); **non-deposit-taking NBFCs** (not HFCs) with assets of **Rs 500 crore and above**.

**Inter-creditor agreement (ICA)** during the Review Period for borrowers with **more than one specified lender**:

- A decision by signatories with **75 per cent by value** of total outstanding credit facilities (**fund based and non-fund based**) **and 60 per cent by number** **binds all**.
- Plans must pay **dissenting signatories at least the liquidation value**.
- The ICA also covers rights and duties of **majority** signatories, protection of **dissenting** signatories, and lenders with **priority in cash flows** or differential security.

**Liquidation value:** the **estimated realisable value of assets** if the borrower were **liquidated on the day the Review Period begins**.
items.expanded_explanation_md: Both tests (value and number) must be met for a binding decision.

self_check.prompt_text: What share by value and by number of signatories makes an ICA decision binding on all?
self_check.expected_takeaway: 75 per cent by value and 60 per cent by number.

items.title: Resolution plan and independent credit evaluation
items.core_explanation_md:
A **resolution plan (RP)** may be **any action, plan or reorganisation**: **regularisation** by paying all overdues, **sale of exposures**, **change in ownership**, **restructuring**. It must be **documented** even if no terms change.

**Independent credit evaluation (ICE)** of the **residual debt** is required for an RP involving **restructuring or change in ownership** where aggregate exposure is **Rs 100 crore and above**, by **credit rating agencies authorised by RBI**.

| Aggregate exposure | ICEs needed |
| --- | --- |
| **Rs 100 crore to below Rs 500 crore** | **One** |
| **Rs 500 crore and above** | **Two** |

**RP symbols:** **RP1** (highest safety, lowest risk) down to **RP7** (very high risk of default). **Only RP4 or better** from **every** required agency lets a plan go ahead. The **lenders engage and pay** the agencies directly.

**Meanwhile**, **normal asset classification continues**; **re-classification does not stop** because an RP is under consideration.
items.expanded_explanation_md: An ICE is different from the ordinary rating needed for an upgrade after restructuring.

self_check.prompt_text: What is the weakest ICE symbol that still allows a resolution plan to proceed?
self_check.expected_takeaway: RP4.

items.title: When an RP is implemented, and additional provisioning if it is late
items.core_explanation_md:
**An RP is "implemented" when**

| RP type | Test |
| --- | --- |
| **No restructuring or change in ownership** | The borrower is **not in default with any specified lender on the 180th day** from the end of the Review Period (a later default is a **fresh default**) |
| **Restructuring or change in ownership** | **Documentation, security charge and perfection done**; new capital structure or terms **in the books of all lenders and the borrower**; borrower **not in default** |
| **Exit by assignment, or recovery action** | The exposure is **fully extinguished** |

**Deadline:** within **180 days from the end of the Review Period** for large accounts (reference dates **7 June 2019** for **Rs 2,000 crore and above**, **1 January 2020** for **Rs 1,500 crore to below Rs 2,000 crore**).

**Additional specific provisions if a viable RP is not implemented in time**

| Timeline missed | Additional provision (% of total outstanding, fund and non-fund based) |
| --- | --- |
| **180 days** from the end of the Review Period | **20 per cent** |
| **365 days** from the start of the Review Period | **15 per cent more** (total **35 per cent**) |

These come **over and above the higher** of provisions held and provisions needed on classification, with **total provisions capped at 100 per cent**. They are also needed once **recovery proceedings** start, unless completed.

**Reversal:** **payment of overdues only**: after **six months without default**; **restructuring or ownership change outside IBC**: on **implementation**; **under IBC**: **half on filing, the rest on admission**; **assignment or recovery**: on **completion**.
items.expanded_explanation_md: Accounts below Rs 1,500 crore are outside this additional provisioning chapter.

self_check.prompt_text: What total additional provision applies if a viable RP is still not implemented 365 days after the start of the Review Period?
self_check.expected_takeaway: 35 per cent (20 per cent plus 15 per cent) of total outstanding.

items.title: Additional provisioning for a delayed resolution plan
items.core_explanation_md: A borrower has total outstanding (fund based and non-fund based) of Rs 800 crore. Provisions already held are Rs 120 crore and the provisions required on its asset classification are Rs 200 crore. A viable resolution plan is not implemented within 180 days from the end of the Review Period, and later not within 365 days from the start of the Review Period. Find the additional provisions at each stage and the total provisions.

worked_steps.description: The base is the higher of provisions held and provisions required.
At 180 days: additional 20 per cent of total outstanding.
Total provisions at this stage (cap: 100 per cent of Rs 800 crore).
At 365 days: a further 15 per cent, so 35 per cent in all.
Total provisions at this stage.
worked_steps.intermediate_result: Rs 480 crore (below the Rs 800 crore cap)

items.final_answer_with_unit: Additional provisions of Rs 160 crore at 180 days and Rs 280 crore in all at 365 days; total provisions Rs 360 crore and then Rs 480 crore, within the cap of Rs 800 crore

self_check.prompt_text: If the provision required on classification were Rs 600 crore, what would the total provisions be at 365 days?
self_check.expected_takeaway: The cap of Rs 800 crore: 600 + 280 = 880 is capped at 100 per cent of the outstanding.

items.title: Prudential norms after restructuring and upgradation
items.core_explanation_md:
**Classification after restructuring**

- A **standard** account is **immediately downgraded to NPA** (sub-standard to begin with).
- An **NPA stays in the same category**. Ageing norms continue to apply.

**Additional finance:** may be **standard during the monitoring period** if the account performs satisfactorily; if not, it takes the **restructured debt's category**. **Interim finance under the IBC** may be **standard** during the insolvency resolution process.

**Periods**

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Monitoring period** | From RP implementation until at least **10 per cent** of the **outstanding principal debt plus capitalised interest** is repaid |
| **Specified period** | Until at least **20 per cent** of that sum is repaid |

**Upgrade of a restructured NPA**

- **All facilities** show **satisfactory performance** (**no default with any specified lender**) during the **monitoring period**.
- **Not before one year** from the **first payment** of interest or principal on the facility with the **longest moratorium**.
- For **Rs 100 crore and above**: facilities also **rated investment grade (BBB minus or better)** at upgrade: **one rating below Rs 500 crore, two at Rs 500 crore and above**. These are **normal ratings, not ICE**.
- **Default after upgrade** within the specified period needs a **fresh resolution plan**.

**Income:** **accrual** for restructured **standard** accounts; **cash basis** for **NPAs**.

**MSMEs with exposure under Rs 25 crore** (commercial banks): **satisfactory performance** means **no payment outstanding for more than 30 days** (for CC or OD, within limit or drawing power for not more than 30 continuous days); **specified period** is **one year** from the first payment.
items.expanded_explanation_md: The monitoring period measures repayment, not calendar time.

self_check.prompt_text: What share of outstanding principal and capitalised interest must be repaid to end the monitoring period?
self_check.expected_takeaway: At least 10 per cent.

items.title: Monitoring period and specified period after a restructuring
items.core_explanation_md: A restructuring plan leaves outstanding principal debt of Rs 500 crore and capitalised interest of Rs 50 crore. Find the repayment needed to end the monitoring period and the specified period, and the number of ratings needed for an upgrade if aggregate exposure at implementation is Rs 120 crore and if it is Rs 620 crore.

worked_steps.description: Base = outstanding principal debt + capitalised interest.
Monitoring period ends at 10 per cent repaid.
Specified period ends at 20 per cent repaid.
Exposure of Rs 120 crore is above Rs 100 crore but below Rs 500 crore: one investment grade rating.
Exposure of Rs 620 crore is Rs 500 crore and above: two ratings, all investment grade.

items.final_answer_with_unit: Monitoring period ends after Rs 55 crore is repaid and the specified period after Rs 110 crore; one rating for a Rs 120 crore exposure and two for Rs 620 crore, all investment grade (BBB minus or better)

self_check.expected_takeaway: No: the account cannot be upgraded before one year from the commencement of the first payment of interest or principal on the facility with the longest moratorium.

items.title: Change in ownership and accounts ineligible for restructuring
items.core_explanation_md:
**Change in ownership** (under the **IBC** or the **Resolution Directions**) lets facilities **continue or be upgraded as standard**. Under the Directions the conditions are:

1. **Due diligence**: the acquirer is **not disqualified under section 29A of the IBC**.
2. The **new promoter** is **not from the existing promoter group** and not its **subsidiary or associate**.
3. The new promoter holds **at least 26 per cent** of **paid-up equity and voting rights** and is the **single largest shareholder**.
4. The new promoter is in **control** (as defined in the Companies Act, SEBI rules or accounting standards).
5. The **RP implementation conditions** are met.

Then **all loans** must show **satisfactory performance** with **all specified lenders** during the **monitoring period**; **failure triggers a fresh Review Period**. **Provisions** (excluding additional provisions) can be **reversed only after the monitoring period** with satisfactory performance.

**Ineligible for restructuring:** borrowers who committed **fraud, malfeasance or wilful default**, and **entities associated with a wilful defaulter**.

**Exceptions:** where **existing promoters are replaced by new promoters** meeting the conditions and the company is **fully delinked** from the old promoters, the bank may take a view on viability (criminal action continues); a wilful defaulter becomes **eligible after its name is removed** from the List of Wilful Defaulters, subject to the penal measures.
items.expanded_explanation_md: The 26 per cent and single-largest-shareholder tests ensure real control passes to the new promoter.

self_check.prompt_text: What minimum stake must a new promoter acquire for standard classification after a change in ownership under the Directions?
self_check.expected_takeaway: At least 26 per cent of paid-up equity capital and voting rights, as the single largest shareholder.

items.title: Projects under implementation: DCCO deferment, cost overrun and change in scope
items.core_explanation_md:
A **credit event** with any lender in the **construction phase** triggers **collective resolution** (with "default" read as "credit event"), reported to **CRILC** and to other **consortium members**.

**A standard project finance account stays standard** after an **RP that defers the DCCO** if it meets:

| Condition | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| **Permitted deferment** | **Up to 3 years** for **infrastructure**; **up to 2 years** for **non-infrastructure** (including CRE and CRE-RH); repayment shift for **equal or shorter** duration |
| **Cost overrun** | Up to **10 per cent** of **original project cost** (plus interest during construction), funded by a **standby credit facility** sanctioned at **financial closure** and **renewed without a gap**; debt equity ratio and external rating **unchanged or better for the bank** |
| **Change in scope and size** | Rise in cost **excluding cost overrun** is **25 per cent or more** of the original outlay; **viability reassessed**; external rating **not more than one notch lower**; benefit **only once** in the project's life |

**Within 180 days** of the end of the Review Period the **documentation and new capital structure** must be in the books, or the account is **downgraded to NPA immediately**. It can be **upgraded** only after **satisfactory performance after actual DCCO** (or, for a miss on the 180-day conditions, on **successful RP implementation** with no further deferment request).

**Provisioning:** **0.375 per cent (infrastructure)** and **0.5625 per cent (non-infrastructure, CRE, CRE-RH)** of the **funded outstanding for each quarter of deferment**, **over and above** the standard asset provision; **reversed** when commercial operations **commence**.

**Existing projects** (financial closure **before 1 October 2025**) follow the **earlier rules** unless there is a **fresh credit event or change in material terms** after that date.
items.expanded_explanation_md: The courseware's older deferment table (adding one or two years for promoter-independent delays) is not part of the 2025 text.

self_check.prompt_text: What is the permitted DCCO deferment for a non-infrastructure project?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Up to 2 years from the original DCCO.

items.title: Projects under implementation: provisioning and scope tests
items.core_explanation_md: An infrastructure project loan has a funded outstanding of Rs 1,000 crore and its DCCO is deferred by two quarters. A non-infrastructure project loan with a funded outstanding of Rs 1,000 crore is deferred by three quarters. A separate project originally cost Rs 1,000 crore and now costs Rs 1,400 crore, of which Rs 100 crore is cost overrun and the rest is for change in scope. Find the additional provisions for each deferment and whether the scope change qualifies.

worked_steps.description: Infrastructure: 0.375 per cent per quarter of deferment.
Non-infrastructure: 0.5625 per cent per quarter of deferment.
Cost attributable to change in scope = total rise - cost overrun.
As a share of the original cost.
The 25 per cent test.

items.final_answer_with_unit: Additional provisions Rs 7.5 crore (infrastructure) and Rs 16.875 crore (non-infrastructure); the change in scope is 30.00 per cent of the original cost, so it qualifies

self_check.prompt_text: Would a rise in scope costing Rs 240 crore on an original Rs 1,000 crore qualify?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No: 24 per cent is below 25 per cent.

items.title: Sale and transfer of stressed loans
items.core_explanation_md:
**Stressed loans** are loans classified as **NPA or SMA**.

**How:** only by **assignment or novation** (**no loan participation**).

**Policy and valuation:** Board policy on **procedure, valuation, delegation and risk premium**; **top-down** identification; NPAs above a threshold **reviewed periodically**. If the exposure (without netting provisions) is **Rs 100 crore or more**, get **two external valuation reports**.

**To whom and how**

- **Permitted transferees:** **scheduled commercial banks**, **all India financial institutions**, **small finance banks**, **NBFCs including HFCs**, and **ARCs**.
- **E-auction** platforms may be used.
- **Bilateral negotiation** must be followed by a **Swiss Challenge** auction where aggregate lender exposure is **Rs 100 crore or more**. The policy fixes the **minimum mark-up of the challenger bid over the base bid**: **not less than 5 per cent and not more than 15 per cent**.

**Rules for the transferor**

- **No contingent price**.
- To **non-ARC** transferees: **cash**, with the **whole consideration at transfer**.
- Price **below NBV (funded outstanding less specific provisions)**: **shortfall debited to P&L**; **above NBV**: **excess provisions may be reversed**.
- **No further risk or funding**; **fresh exposure** only after a **cooling period of at least 12 months**.

**Rules for an acquiring bank**

- With **no existing exposure** to the borrower: classify as **standard** at acquisition.
- **Provision** for any shortfall of the **NPV of estimated cash flows** against the **price paid**, discounting at the **original contract rate plus a risk premium of at least 3 per cent**.
- **Hold for at least six months** before transferring on.
items.expanded_explanation_md: A resolution plan exit approved by the 75 and 60 per cent ICA majority makes the Swiss Challenge compulsory whatever the size.

self_check.prompt_text: What is the permitted range of the minimum mark-up over the base bid in a Swiss Challenge?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Not less than 5 per cent and not more than 15 per cent.

items.title: Sale of a stressed loan below net book value, and a Swiss Challenge
items.core_explanation_md: A bank has a stressed loan with funded outstanding of Rs 100 crore and provisions of Rs 60 crore. It negotiates a cash sale for Rs 30 crore. Separately, a base bid of Rs 200 crore is received for another stressed loan and the bank's policy sets a minimum mark-up of 8 per cent for the challenger bid. A buyer that has no existing exposure acquires a stressed loan for Rs 50 crore, with the NPV of estimated cash flows at Rs 44 crore. Find the shortfall debited to the profit and loss account, the minimum challenger bid, and the provision the buyer makes.

worked_steps.description: NBV = funded outstanding - specific provisions.
Price is below NBV; the shortfall goes to the profit and loss account.
Minimum challenger bid = base bid x (1 + mark-up).
Buyer provides for NPV below the consideration paid.

items.final_answer_with_unit: Shortfall of Rs 10 crore debited to profit and loss; minimum challenger bid Rs 216 crore; the buyer provides Rs 6 crore

self_check.prompt_text: What range of challenger bids would a policy mark-up between 5 and 15 per cent allow on a Rs 200 crore base bid?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Between Rs 210 crore and Rs 230 crore, depending on the mark-up the policy fixes.

items.title: Transfers to ARCs and transfers of borrower accounts
items.core_explanation_md:
**To an asset reconstruction company (ARC):** any stressed loan **in default** may be transferred.

- **Price below NBV:** **shortfall to P&L**; **floating or countercyclical provisions may be used**.
- **Price above NBV:** **excess provision reversed only as cash received exceeds NBV**.
- **Security receipts (SRs):** valued on the **NAV** the ARC declares from **recovery ratings**; SRs **unredeemed at the end of the resolution period (five or eight years)** are **loss assets**, fully provided.
- A bank may **take over a standard account from an ARC** after a period equal to the **monitoring period**, if the account **performed satisfactorily**.

**Transfer of a borrower account at the borrower's request (take-over)**

- **Board approved policy:** **which accounts**, **authority levels**, **reporting to higher authority**, **monitoring**, **credit audit**, **staff accountability for quick mortality**, **periodic Board or Committee review**.
- **Before take-over**, the **transferee bank obtains credit information** from the **transferor bank** in the **prescribed format**, so it knows any **irregularities**.
- The **transferor** shares the information **at the earliest** on request.
items.expanded_explanation_md: This replaces the courseware's account of the 2012 circular on transfer of borrowal accounts.

self_check.prompt_text: What must the transferee bank obtain before taking over a borrower's account from another bank?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Credit information from the transferor bank in the prescribed format.

items.title: The Code, who it covers and who runs it
items.core_explanation_md:
**IBC 2016** puts the laws on reorganisation and insolvency into **one Code**.

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Insolvency** | **Liabilities exceed assets**; cannot pay debts |
| **Bankruptcy** | **Legal recognition** of insolvency **beyond resolution**; a **trustee** sells property and discharges obligations |

| Part | Applies to |
| --- | --- |
| **Part II** | **Companies and LLPs** (**corporate debtors**), **personal guarantors** to them, and other bodies the Government notifies |
| **Part III** | **Partnership and proprietorship concerns** and **individuals** |

**The ecosystem**

- **IBBI:** the **regulator** (of **insolvency professionals, agencies, entities and information utilities**).
- **Insolvency professionals:** **IRP, RP, liquidator, bankruptcy trustee**.
- **Information utilities:** hold **financial information** and the **certificate of default**.
- **Financial creditors:** **lent money** (time value). **Operational creditors:** supplied **goods or services on credit**, or took **advances** for them.
- **Committee of creditors (CoC).**
- **Courts:** **NCLT** and **NCLAT** (corporate), **DRT** and **DRAT** (individuals and partnerships), **Supreme Court**.
items.expanded_explanation_md: The courseware stresses that the Code is a consolidation, which is why it is called a Code rather than an Act.

self_check.prompt_text: Which tribunal is the adjudicating authority for corporate debtors?
self_check.expected_takeaway: The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT), with NCLAT for appeals.

items.title: From debtors in possession to creditors in control
items.core_explanation_md:
**Before the Code:** the **debtor stayed in possession** and the creditor chased it through many laws.

**Under the Code:**

1. On **appointment of the IRP**, the **board's powers are suspended** and the IRP takes over as **CEO**.
2. When the **committee of creditors** is formed, it **supersedes the board**.
3. **Original promoters and their related parties** cannot bid for the **corporate debtor** (**section 29A**): ownership, control and management leave the existing promoters.

The courseware calls the Code **debtor-friendly** in one sense: it asks whether the **business can be revived**, treating the **business separately from its promoters**.
items.expanded_explanation_md: The pre-pack reverses part of this: the debtor stays in management while a base plan is prepared.

self_check.prompt_text: What happens to the powers of the board of directors when the IRP is appointed?
self_check.expected_takeaway: They are suspended and the IRP takes over the management.
